purpose: Evaluate evidence-backed web experience quality across declared critical states and responsive viewports without inventing browser observations or visual thresholds.
activate_when: A web UI change has user-visible layout, interaction-state, responsive, accessibility or visual-regression risk.
A Delivery Mission claims preview or production web experience quality that requires browser-observed evidence.

evidence: Observed critical-state behavior and accessibility structure in a real browser.
Screenshot or equivalent rendered visual evidence for every declared visual case.

entry_points.purpose: Evaluate declared critical-state, responsive, accessibility and visual-discrepancy evidence and return PASS, FAIL or INCOMPLETE.

failure_modes: A required critical state or viewport has no observation.
Browser interaction for a required case failed or was not run.
Required accessibility evidence failed or is absent.
A blocker or material visual discrepancy remains unresolved.
Visual evidence was captured in an unstable or incomparable environment and cannot support the claim.
recovery_actions: Capture or rerun the missing required case in the resolved browser/visual tool surface.
Correct the UI or accessibility defect and submit a new observation linked to the declared case.
Resolve material discrepancies with a new evidence iteration rather than weakening the acceptance claim.
If rendering conditions are not comparable, recapture baseline and actual evidence under a controlled common environment.
stop_conditions: Required browser or visual-capture capability is unavailable.
A required case cannot be exercised without unavailable authorization or data.
Evidence is insufficient to distinguish a real visual defect from an unstable capture environment.
